notes: Passage-checked from the online Sanskrit text and verse-by-verse English gloss/translation hosted by SanskritDocuments.org. Chapter pages do not identify the print edition; Sanskrit śloka locators are retained as 6-kanda.sarga.verse.

Sargas 26–27 contain Śaraṇa’s roster of named commanders in the monkey/bear host. Sarga 43 supplies individually named battlefield opponents and direct duel/defeat claims. There are 50 source-local person records including seven reused graph anchors and 43 newly source-scoped records; the unresolved Sarga 27 Rambha/Dambha mention is kept separate from Sarga 26 Rambha.
No troop counts, army collectives, places, or unnamed commanders are represented as people. Dhumra and Jāmbavān are bear leaders; most other chiefs are explicitly monkeys.

Aṅgada here is Vāli’s son, not the later Aṅgada listed in Viṣṇu Purāṇa 4.4 as Lakṣmaṇa’s son. The monkey combatant Sampāti is kept separate from the vulture Sampāti. The rākṣasa Śatrughna is kept separate from Rāma’s brother.

For Sarga 27, 6.27.15–16, the IAST verse reads Rambha, while the page’s word-gloss and translation give Dambha. This unresolved mention has a separate source-local node and is not identified with Sarga 26 Rambha.

Clear existing graph IDs reused: Rāma (`rama`), Sugrīva (`sugriva`), Lakṣmaṇa (`lakshmana`), Rāvaṇa (`ravana_epic`), Vibhīṣaṇa (`vibhishana_epic`), Indra (`indra`), Dharma (`vp20_dharma_deity`). No Agastya occurrence is in these roster verses.
